dossier:
Spain didn't just win the 2010 World Cup in South Africa — they rewired football's DNA. That tournament, built on tiki-taka and a philosophy that said *possession is power*, gave the world Iniesta's extra-time winner against the Netherlands and a generation of players who grew up believing football should be played on the ground, between the lines, with purpose. One title. One golden summer. Sixteen years of living off it, and still, nobody pulls on that red shirt without feeling its weight.

The years between then and now haven't always been kind. Spain have turned up to tournaments with squads full of talent and gone home early with excuses. But Euro 2024 felt like a rebirth — fluid, young, electric. That tournament introduced the world to Nico Williams and confirmed that Pedri is generational, a midfielder who plays football the way great writers use silence: knowing exactly what not to do.

Now they arrive at 2026 with genuine hunger and a squad ranked third in the world. The bones of a champion are here — tactical intelligence, technical purity, and something Spain hasn't always had: genuine pace and chaos on the flanks. The question isn't whether they can play beautiful football. It's whether they can finally marry beauty to brutality when the knockout rounds bite back.
whatToWatch: Watch Spain for Lamine Yamal — a teenager who plays with the kind of arrogance and artistry that only comes along once a decade, making full-backs look like they're running in sand. When he and Nico Williams both get going on opposite flanks, it's the most exciting 90 minutes club football can't buy you.
xFactor: Lamine Yamal — still a teenager but already playing like someone who's read every great winger's autobiography and decided to write a better one, and if he catches fire in North America, this will be remembered as the tournament where the world finally understood what the fuss was about.
verdict: Spain will play the prettiest football of anyone in the competition and either break your heart in a quarterfinal or remind you exactly why they once made the whole world fall in love with them.
funFacts: Spain's 2010 World Cup triumph came with a record low of just two goals conceded across seven matches — defence, not just that famous flair, won them the trophy.
Lamine Yamal was born on 13 May 2007, meaning he was literally born the same day Lionel Messi played his first Champions League final — the football gods clearly planned something.
name: Spain
